displayedInputs.question:
Circle \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) each have radius \(1,\) and the distance between their centers is \(\frac{1}{2}.\) Circle \(C_3\) is the largest circle internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2.\) Circle \(C_4\) is internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) and externally tangent to \(C_3.\) What is the radius of \(C_4?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Six regular hexagonal blocks of side length \(1\) unit are arranged inside a regular hexagonal frame. Each block lies along an inside edge of the frame and is aligned with two other blocks, as shown in the figure below. The distance from any corner of the frame to the nearest vertex of a block is \(\frac{3}{7}\) unit. What is the area of the region inside the frame not occupied by the blocks?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Square \(ABCD\) is rotated \(20^\circ\) clockwise about its center to obtain square \(EFGH,\) as shown below. What is the degree measure of \(\angle EAB?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Four congruent semicircles are drawn on the surface of a sphere with radius \(2,\) as shown, creating a closed curve that divides the surface into two congruent regions. The length of the curve is \(\pi\sqrt{n}.\) What is \(n?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

A square of area \(2\) is inscribed in a square of area \(3,\) creating four congruent triangles, as shown below. What is the ratio of the shorter leg to the longer leg in the shaded right triangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Usain is walking for exercise by zigzagging across a \(100\)-meter by \(30\)-meter rectangular field, beginning at point \(A\) and ending on the segment \(\overline{BC}.\) He wants to increase the distance walked by zigzagging as shown in the figure below (\(APQRS\)). What angle \(\theta=\angle PAB\) \(=\angle QPC\) \(=\angle RQB=\cdots\) will produce a length that is \(120\) meters? (Do not assume the zigzag path has exactly four segments as shown; there could be more or fewer.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Circle \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) each have radius \(1,\) and the distance between their centers is \(\tfrac12.\) Circle \(C_3\) is the largest circle internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2.\) Circle \(C_4\) is internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) and externally tangent to \(C_3.\) What is the radius of \(C_4?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

A square piece of paper is folded twice into four equal quarters, as shown below, then cut along the dashed line. When unfolded, the paper will match which of the following figures?

mappings.rationale: Internal tangency gives differences of radii as center distances, while external tangency gives their sum. The equidistant-center locus supplies the right triangle used to determine the unknown radius.
mappings.answerReason: Let M be the midpoint of the original centers. The largest inner circle is centered at M with radius 3/4. For C4 of radius r, its center is 3/4+r from M and 1−r from either original center, so (1/4)²+(3/4+r)²=(1−r)². This gives r=3/28.

mappings.rationale: Aligned parallel block edges determine the frame side. Each regular hexagon's area can then be computed using its apothem and six triangular sectors, and the occupied areas subtracted.
mappings.answerReason: Write d=3/7. Alignment of neighboring block edges makes the three portions of a frame edge d, 1, and 2−d, so the frame side is 3. A regular hexagon of side t has area 3√3·t²/2; therefore the unoccupied area is (3√3/2)(9−6)=9√3/2.

mappings.rationale: Rotation preserves distances to the center and gives a 20° central angle between corresponding vertices. Square diagonal geometry then supports either an isosceles-triangle calculation or an inscribed-angle calculation.
mappings.answerReason: With O the center, OA=OE and ∠AOE=20°, so ∠EAO=(180°−20°)/2=80°. Since ∠OAB=45°, the requested angle is 80°−45°=35°.

mappings.rationale: The depicted symmetric seam reduces the semicircle-radius calculation to the side and diagonal of a square in a central section. The total curve length is then the sum of four semicircular arc lengths, not a sphere-area calculation.
mappings.answerReason: In the smooth symmetric configuration shown, the four semicircle diameters form a square in a central section of the sphere. Its diagonal is 4, so its side is 2√2 and each semicircle has radius √2. The total length is 4π√2=π√32, giving n=32.
limitations: The central-square step uses the smooth, symmetric seam depicted; the text does not independently specify the planes of the semicircles.

mappings.rationale: The target is the shorter-to-longer leg ratio. The outer square fixes the sum of the legs; either the triangle areas determine their product, or the inner-square side determines their squared-length sum.
mappings.answerReason: For legs a≤b, the square sides give a+b=√3 and a²+b²=2. Thus ab=1/2 and (b−a)²=1. Consequently a/b=(√3−1)/(√3+1)=2−√3.

mappings.rationale: Every path segment has the same cosine relative to the long side, so its forward projection is its length times cos θ. Summing these projections, or unfolding the reflections into one right triangle, determines the angle.
mappings.answerReason: All segments move forward, and their horizontal projections total 100 meters. Thus 120 cos θ=100, giving cos θ=5/6 and θ=arccos(5/6). This also accounts for any final partial segment.

mappings.rationale: Internal and external circle tangency translate into center-distance equations. Equal distances to the two original centers place the unknown center on their perpendicular bisector.
mappings.answerReason: The largest inner circle has center at the midpoint M of the original centers and radius 3/4. If C4 has radius r, the relevant right triangle has legs 1/4 and 3/4+r and hypotenuse 1−r. Hence (1/4)²+(3/4+r)²=(1−r)², which yields r=3/28.

mappings.rationale: Unfolding reconstructs the cut by successive reflections across the two perpendicular crease lines. This is a reflected-image task, not a length calculation involving folded quadrilaterals.
mappings.derivedAnswer: E, the square with a central diamond-shaped hole
mappings.answerReason: The cut removes the corner where the two folds meet, which corresponds to the center of the original sheet. Reflecting the diagonal cut across both creases produces four sides of a central diamond-shaped hole while leaving the outer square unchanged.
